title: RISED: Rubrics for Agentic Multi-Environment Selection and Self-Distillation
gist: Apple ML Research paper RISED uses an LLM judge to tag rollouts with a shared rubric vocabulary and uses those rubrics for online data selection, on-policy self-distillation and negative-rubric rollout steering when training one agent across multiple RL environments. It reports the highest mean pass rate across environments and first or second rank in every environment.

insights.claim: Training one LLM agent jointly across diverse interactive environments is an increasingly pursued route to generalist agents.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Generalist-agent training recipes are an active frontier; watch for adoption by frontier labs.

insights.claim: Existing curriculum and data-selection strategies allocate training at the environment level or prioritize local reward signals, without considering relationships between rollouts across environments for prompt-group selection.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Identifies a gap in current multi-environment RL data selection.

insights.claim: Because environments are learned at different rates, all-failure and all-success rollout groups coexist within a batch and provide no group-relative reward signal when rewards are identical.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Explains wasted compute in GRPO-style training with scalar rewards.
insights.locator: as environments are learned at different rates

insights.claim: RISED repurposes rubrics beyond reward use: an LLM judge tags each rollout with a predefined rubric vocabulary shared across environments, and the profiles guide online selection of data matching the batch's behavioural composition while limiting overlap with already-selected data.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Rubric-tagged rollouts become a data-curation primitive, not just a reward signal.
insights.locator: An LLM judge tags each rollout

insights.claim: Positive rubrics describing desired behaviours serve as privileged context for an on-policy self-distillation teacher, giving token-level supervision, while negative rubrics steer later rollout generation away from recurring failure modes.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Combines textual feedback with distillation to extract signal where scalar rewards are flat.

insights.claim: Richer textual feedback such as rubrics describing rollout behaviours is motivated by scalar rewards carrying limited information about cross-environment relationships.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Part of a broader shift from scalar to rubric-based rewards in post-training.

insights.claim: Across model backbones, RISED achieves the highest mean pass rate across environments and ranks first or second in every individual environment.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Abstract-level claim with no numbers given; treat as unverified until the paper's tables are checked.
insights.quote: RISED achieves the highest mean pass rate across environments and ranks first or second in every individual environment.

insights.claim: Rubric-based analysis of RISED can characterize the behavioural changes that accompany its gains.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Rubrics double as an interpretability tool for agent training.
